title: A Compass for the Regiment
premise: In 1848, apprentice clockmaker Emrys Dravenmoor is summoned to the mountain observatory to repair its failing master clock, only to find a stranger waiting with letters in the handwriting of Colonel Aldous Vane — the regiment's celebrated war hero, officially dead for six years. The colonel lives, hidden and disgraced, and his letters reveal that the regiment's founding charter, which grants its commanders near-feudal power over the valley, was forged. Emrys, whose late father helped forge it, must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the family name he barely knows. As the current commander hunts the 'corpse' to destroy the evidence, Emrys smuggles Vane's testimony toward the capital, discovering along the way that identity is not what history assigns us but what we dare to claim. The novel ends at the observatory clock: Emrys stops it publicly at the hour of Vane's supposed death, forcing an inquiry that breaks the charter's power, though Vane dies before vindication and Emrys inherits not glory but the burden of telling the truth.
about_author: Tamsin Lockridge is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing regimental records in provincial garrison towns, where she first encountered the paperwork of invented heroes. She writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in machinery far larger than themselves.

chapters.title: The Hour That Will Not Hold
chapters.summary: Emrys Dravenmoor, POV. Summoned from his master's workshop to the mountain observatory, Emrys finds the great master clock losing four minutes a day for no mechanical reason he can diagnose. He resents being sent; history, he believes, happens elsewhere, to other people. Emotional beat: restless competence masking a small, unexamined life.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Cold Hands
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. A gaunt stranger arrives at dusk asking for the clockmaker by name, though no one knew Emrys was coming. He carries oilcloth-wrapped letters bearing the unmistakable hand of Colonel Aldous Vane — dead six years, hero of the regiment. Emotional beat: dread arriving politely, disguised as a request.

chapters.title: Handwriting of a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. The stranger, Pell, claims Vane lives in hiding and wants the letters placed inside the master clock's case — the one place the commander's men will never search, because they fear the mechanism. Emrys refuses, then recognizes his own father's marginal corrections on a draft. Emotional beat: refusal curdling into complicity.

chapters.title: What My Father Signed
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV, with flashback. Sorting his father's effects, Emrys finds drafting tools, practice strokes matching the charter's script, and a payment ledger from the regiment. His father helped forge the founding charter that grants the commanders their power. Emotional beat: grief reassembling itself as betrayal.

chapters.title: The Commander's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Commander Halewick, POV. The regiment's commander receives Emrys warmly, shows off the restored observatory, and mentions — lightly — that Pell was seen on the valley road. Halewick is charming, generous, and utterly certain of his right to rule. Emotional beat: menace wearing the mask of hospitality.

chapters.title: Four Minutes of Silence
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Emrys hides the letters inside the clock's weight channel and discovers why the clock loses time: someone has been deliberately slowing it for years, marking hours when the observatory was dark — signals, or alibis. Emotional beat: the machine becomes a witness.

chapters.title: Letters from a Living Grave
chapters.summary: Vane, POV (his letters, read by Emrys). Vane's account reveals he discovered the forgery, refused to endorse it, and was declared dead after a staged ambush. He writes not of vengeance but of a promise made in peacetime to Emrys's father. Emotional beat: honor surviving disgrace.

chapters.title: The Promise in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV, flashback. A memory surfaces: age nine, a kind officer teaching him to cut gears, making him promise that if ever asked, he would tell the time truly. He never understood until now. Emotional beat: childhood oath becoming adult duty.

chapters.title: Roadblock at the Ford
chapters.summary: Pell, POV. Taking the secondary road to the capital with copied testimony, Pell is stopped at the ford by soldiers checking papers. He escapes by river but loses the satchel — which contains nothing, a decoy he prepared. Emotional beat: cunning stretched thin over fear.

chapters.title: The Search of the Observatory
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Halewick's men search the observatory room by room while Emrys keeps them talking beside the running clock, terrified they will hear the faint rustle of paper in the weights. They leave empty-handed. Emotional beat: terror conducted at conversational volume.

chapters.title: An Ally with Her Own Reasons
chapters.summary: Isolde Marchmont, POV. The observatory's astronomer, Isolde, reveals she has known about the slowed clock for two years and has been recording the falsified hours. She offers her star-charts as independent proof — she has her own grievance against the charter. Emotional beat: solitude ending in wary alliance.

chapters.title: The Charter Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Halewick, POV. At the regiment's founding-day feast, Halewick reads the charter aloud as tradition demands, and Emrys, seated among the guests, hears the forged clauses in his father's cadences. Halewick catches Emrys's expression. Emotional beat: public ceremony, private indictment.

chapters.title: A Meeting Above the Snowline
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Guided by Pell, Emrys climbs to Vane's hiding place — a ruined chapel — and meets the living legend: older, ill, unbowed. Vane asks not for rescue but for a true clock in the observatory, so the record of hours can be trusted again. Emotional beat: awe giving way to intimacy.

chapters.title: The Trap Baited with Mercy
chapters.summary: Halewick, POV. Halewick offers Emrys his father's debts forgiven and a master's certificate if he surrenders the letters, framing it as protection from treason charges. Emrys asks for a night to decide. Emotional beat: corruption offering itself as kindness.

chapters.title: What Emrys Decides
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Alone with the clock at midnight, Emrys weighs safety against the promise, his father's shame against his own name. He repairs the clock to perfect time — erasing the false slowness — and sends word to Vane: the record will be honest. Emotional beat: quiet, irreversible choice.

chapters.title: Flight Down the Valley
chapters.summary: Isolde, POV. With the clock corrected, Halewick realizes the observatory has turned against him. Soldiers move at dawn; Isolde smuggles Emrys out through the instrument tunnels with the original draft hidden in a telescope tube. Emotional beat: flight sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: The Decoy Burns
chapters.summary: Pell, POV. Captured with the decoy satchel, Pell lets Halewick believe he has won, buying three days while the real testimony travels with a grain merchant. In his cell, Pell measures his remaining courage in hours. Emotional beat: sacrifice disguised as defeat.

chapters.title: The Inquiry Arrives
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. An inspector from the capital, prompted by Isolde's mailed charts, arrives to investigate irregularities in the regimental records. Halewick produces the burned decoy as proof of conspiracy against him. Emotional beat: hope entangled in a liar's counterattack.

chapters.title: The Clock Stops
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Before the assembled regiment, Emrys stops the master clock at the exact hour of Vane's supposed death and opens the case, producing the original draft and Vane's letters. He names his father's part in the forgery first. Emotional beat: climax — truth told at cost, including to himself.

chapters.title: Halewick's Last Inspection
chapters.summary: Halewick, POV. Cornered, Halewick attempts to seize the observatory by force, insisting the charter makes him law. His own officers, hearing the evidence, refuse the order. He is taken quietly, still protesting his inheritance of a righteous lie. Emotional beat: power collapsing into pettiness.

chapters.title: Vindication, Too Late
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV. Word comes that Vane died in the chapel the night the inquiry began, holding the promise letter. The regiment restores his name; Emrys is offered honors and declines them, asking instead that the clock be kept honest by whoever serves it next. Emotional beat: victory shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: Setting the Time
chapters.summary: Emrys, POV, one year later. Master clockmaker now, Emrys returns to wind the observatory clock, Isolde beside him. History, he understands at last, happened here all along — to him. He sets the hands to the true hour and lets it run. Emotional beat: resolution — identity claimed, inheritance transformed into responsibility.
